200 bps margin improvement expected from Del Monte-Sundrop merger synergies over 18 months
Management expects 150-225 bps EBITDA margin expansion in FY27, targeting double-digit margins by FY29
ERP integration expected to complete in 12-14 months (June-August 2027)
Integration synergies expected to deliver 100 bps in FY27 and 150-200 bps in FY28

penalties.details: On January 16, Food safety Officer (FSO), Jaipur has picked up a sample of Sundrop Oil and sent it for analysis. The Food Analysis after testing the product declared it as 'misbranded', since the product is having a line 'Healty Oil for Healty People'. Subsequently, the FSO has filed a complaint before the 'Adjudicating Officer and Additional District Magistrate, Jaipur'. In January 2023, the Adjudicating Officer and Additional District Magistrate had decided the complaint and imposed a penalty of INR 50,000 on the Comapny. Subsequently, the Company had filed an appeal against the said order before Food Safety Appellate Tribunal (FSAT), Jaipur. In September 2026, FSAT, Jaipur has dismissed the appeal filed by the Company through its order dated 03.09.2026.
penalties.impact: The Company is preparing to file the appeal against the order dated 10-09-2026 before High Court of Rajasthan. There is no other impact on the financials or operations of the Company.

GST amount of INR.1.05 crores; Penalty INR. 10.70 lakhs. Company filed Appeal before Commissioner (Appeals). During the current quarter, the appeal application was successfully registered on 09.07.2026 and is pending for listing hearing.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Additional Commissioner, Secunderabad Commisionerate, Basheerbagh, Hyderabad
tax_litigation.status: The Company had filed appeal before GSTAT on 17.06.2026. The appeal application was successfully registered on 09.07.2026 and is pending for listing hearing.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: As per previous disclosure, an Order was issued on the grounds that the Company availed the cenvat credit on the excise duty paid at the time of import on Peanut Butter. The Excise authorities conetested that Peanut Butter is exempt and ACD and SAD has been paid and cenvat credit taken. Excise duty INR.1.40 crores; Penalty INR.1.40 crores. The Company filed Appeal before CESTAT on 30.09.2013. CESTAT had set aside the major demand of INR 2,71,96,416/-. The Tribunal has, however, upheld the demand relating to CENVAT on goods written off amounting to INR 9,02,314/- with interest. The Company had filed an appeal before GSTAT on 25.06.2026. During the current quarter, GSTAT issued deficiency memo on 30.09.2026 and the Company is in the process of filing reply to deficiency.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Commissioner, Hyderabad III Commissionerate, Basheerbagh, Hyderabad
tax_litigation.status: The Company had filed an appeal before GSTAT on 25.06.2026. GSTAT issued deficiency memo on 30.09.2026 and the Company is in the process of filing reply to deficiency.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company received a Show Cause Notice (SCN) dated September 29, 2026, based on the scrutiny of GST returns for the FY 2022-23, issued by the Deputy Commissioner (SGST), Sector-7, Ghaziabad I, Uttar Pradesh, under Section 73 of the UPGST/ CGST Act, 2017, the State Tax, Uttar Pradesh Goods and Services Tax, Ghaziabad Zone-1. The stated SCN has raised a GST demand of INR 26,37,65,281.41/- inclusive a penalty of INR 2,39,78,661.93/-.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Deputy Commissioner (SGST), Sector-7, Ghaziabad I, Uttar Pradesh
tax_litigation.status: The Company is in the process of replying to this SCN, demands and the allegations contained therein on the grounds that the stated authority has not considered the GST liability already discharged by the Company on deemed supplies, export under Letter of Undertaking (LUT) and Reverse Charge Mechanism for the contended Financial Year 2022-23.
